name: Triple Zero (000)
summary: Primary emergency number for Police, Fire or Ambulance; calls are free.
caution: Use for emergencies only. A mobile cannot reach the Emergency Call Service where there is no coverage from any mobile network.

name: Emergency Relay Service / National Relay Service (NRS)
summary: Accessible emergency-call pathways for people who are d/Deaf or have hearing or speech difficulty. Use 106 from a TTY/TDD; it is not a general text-message number.
hours: NRS is available 24/7 except Video Relay; Video Relay hours are limited.
caution: Video Relay is not recommended for emergency calls: it cannot be identified/prioritised as emergency and operates only limited hours. Internet/mobile-based relay may be less reliable than 106 and may not identify caller/location. For a TTY, dial 106 first.

name: NSW State Emergency Service (NSW SES)
summary: Emergency assistance for flood, storm or tsunami, including storm/wind/fallen-tree damage. Requests are prioritised.
caution: If anyone is trapped or injured, call 000. The online contact form is not monitored for storm/flood emergencies; call 132 500.

name: Police Assistance Line
summary: Non-urgent police assistance, minor-crime reporting and general enquiries.
caution: For emergencies or a crime in progress, call 000 instead.

name: Poisons Information Centre
summary: Expert phone advice for suspected exposure to poisons, including medicines, chemicals, cleaning products, bites and stings.
caution: Call promptly; do not wait for symptoms. If someone has stopped breathing or collapsed, call 000 for an ambulance.

name: healthdirect helpline
summary: Health advice from a registered nurse for any health concern.
caution: For urgent medical help, call 000.

name: Lifeline crisis support
summary: Confidential crisis support with a trained crisis supporter; text is also available at 0477 13 11 14.
caution: If life is in danger, call 000.

name: 1800RESPECT
summary: National counselling, information and support for people impacted by domestic, family or sexual violence. Text: 0458 737 732; online chat and video call are also offered.
caution: If in immediate danger, call 000. Use a safer device if possible: calls, texts and browsing can leave records. This directory has no quick-exit feature and does not erase browsing history.

name: Kids Helpline
summary: Free, confidential phone and online-chat counselling for children and young people aged 5–25.

name: NSW Mental Health Line
summary: Free statewide advice, triage and connection to NSW Health mental health services; a trained professional completes a brief assessment and recommends appropriate care.
caution: Not a one-off counselling service. If someone is in immediate danger, call 000 or attend an emergency department.
language: For another language, call TIS National 131 450 and ask to be connected. Relay options are listed on the source page.

name: Service NSW — emergencies and natural disasters
summary: Disaster preparation/recovery information, personalised support pathways, relief/grants information and replacement-document help; includes support-hub information.
caution: In an emergency, call 000; for flood/storm/tsunami assistance, call NSW SES 132 500.

name: Temporary and emergency housing / Link2Home
summary: Link2Home helps people who are homeless or at risk of homelessness. For disaster accommodation pathways, contact Service NSW on 13 77 88 or a recovery centre.

name: Legal Aid NSW — Disaster Response Legal Service
summary: Free legal help after bushfire, storm or flood: insurance claims/disputes, tenancy/housing, disaster grants, financial hardship, Centrelink, work rights and documents.

name: Bureau of Meteorology — NSW warnings summary
summary: Official current NSW weather-warning summary; automatically refreshes when warnings are issued.
caution: Read the linked warning in full and follow local emergency-service directions.

name: Bureau of Meteorology — national warning phone service
summary: Latest weather warnings by phone.

name: Live Traffic NSW
summary: Transport for NSW official real-time road incidents, closures and changed conditions; a text-to-speech Traffic Info Line and operator assistance are available.
caution: Always read individual incident advice/restrictions and do not drive into floodwater or a closed road.

name: NSW SES evacuation centres
summary: Current evacuation-centre locations and opening hours; the page also gives evacuation guidance.
caution: Centres open only during emergencies and status changes. Follow evacuation instructions immediately; check routes via Live Traffic. For fires, consult NSW RFS as directed by the page.

name: NSW SES accessibility resources
summary: Flood/storm/tsunami planning resources for low/no hearing or vision, disability/mobility, intellectual disability, mental health conditions, carers and Easy Read; includes Auslan and NRS information.
caution: Create a tailored plan and support network before an emergency; plan backup power/transport for life-sustaining and mobility equipment.

name: NSW SES — household pets emergency planning
summary: Pet evacuation planning and a 3–7-day animal emergency-kit checklist.
caution: Plan to take pets, but evacuation centres may not always be available or suitable for animals; arrange alternative safe options. Assistance animals have separate access guidance.

name: NSW SES — assistance animals emergency planning
summary: Planning guidance and kit checklist for assistance animals during evacuation.
caution: The NSW SES page says people should not be denied transport or evacuation-centre access because of an assistance animal; plan travel and specific animal needs in advance.

name: NSW Government — Get Ready Animals
summary: Emergency planning for companion animals, larger pets, horses and livestock, including a Pet Ready Plan.
caution: Plan safe animal transport and alternative accommodation early. Do not re-enter an unsafe area to retrieve an animal; follow emergency-service directions.

name: Translating and Interpreting Service (TIS National) pathway for NSW mental-health support
summary: Interpreter connection pathway: ask TIS to ring NSW Mental Health Line 1800 011 511.
caution: For immediate danger, call 000 rather than waiting for a support connection.

name: MyFirePlan
summary: NSW RFS online bushfire planning tool. Discuss your household’s leaving triggers, safer destination, routes and what to take before fire threatens.
caution: Leaving early is your safest choice. Do not wait for an official warning to decide when to leave. This tool is for planning, not incident warnings.

name: NSW Rural Fire Service
summary: Official NSW bushfire information, preparation resources and links to current incidents and fire danger ratings.

name: RFS Fires Near Me
summary: Official NSW RFS incident map and fire information. Read the incident advice and follow emergency-service instructions.
caution: Maps may not show every incident or update immediately. Do not wait for a mapped incident before taking protective action.

name: Fire danger ratings and total fire bans
summary: Check the fire danger rating and total fire ban status for your NSW fire area. A rating describes potential fire consequences; it is not a report that a fire has started.

name: RFS bushfire survival plan
summary: Official bushfire survival planning guidance to use with your household and MyFirePlan.

name: HazardWatch
summary: Official interactive hazard-warning map. NSW SES links to HazardWatch for current flood, severe weather and tsunami warnings.
caution: Check the displayed hazard coverage, location, issue time and full warning. A blank map or no displayed warnings does not mean your location is safe.

name: Hazards Near Me NSW
summary: Find the official Hazards Near Me app through the NSW emergency hub and set watch zones for relevant local emergencies.
caution: Keep more than one information channel. Do not rely on receiving an app notification before acting.

name: H5 bird flu — Australian Government
summary: Australian Government H5 bird flu hub: local advice, reporting, wildlife, pets, backyard birds, farms, human health and translated resources. The short address redirects to the Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry campaign.
caution: If you notice sick or dead birds or other animals, do not touch them or get too close. Take photos only if safe, note the location and report it. This is animal-disease reporting, not a human medical emergency line.

name: Get Ready NSW
summary: Official preparation hub: understand your risk, make an emergency plan, pack a kit, know the warnings and plan with neighbours.

name: NSW SES — during an emergency
summary: Official flood, storm and tsunami response hub, with warnings, apps, evacuation information and links to safety guidance.
